what: A dark metal plate lying at a slant inside the element (three) and 10k 2,000 sand grains (5,000 on phone) — plate vibration mode Ψ = ½[cos(mπu)cos(nπv) ± cos(nπu)cos(mπv)] — only grains where |Ψ|·γ(4.5) exceeds 1 jump in a random walk with step size overflow × .0045, and are nudged by .15 toward lower amplitude, so they gather on the nodal lines that do not move. When fx:mode receives a different (m, n, ±), the two patterns blend over 1.4s and the sand migrates to the new lines. Grains that leave the plate are scattered again

options.shape: If “disc”, a disc (m across the diameter × n concentric rings)
options.grains: Number of sand grains, default 12000 (5000 under 768 width)
options.morph: Blend length when the mode changes (sec), default 1.4
options.tilt: Panel tilt from 0 (from above) to 1 (low), default .55
options.fx:mode: Element detail { m, n, sign } Send it and it switches to that mode
options.fx:sprinkle: Sending it scatters the sand across the whole board again

note: The original has a GPU-computed plate (texture 448², 200k sand grains) plus plate bending, brass light and camera presets. Here the parts carry over only the same physics rules, run as a CPU walk — within the site, plate.js also handles bending, light, camera and the frequency sweep. It pauses when off screen.
